messages:
olivia: Quick RFC follow-up: when a tenant announces an on-prem prefix that overlaps our regional relay, how do we pick which path? we need something deterministic and debuggable.
sam: We talked prefer-tenant vs prefer-relay. leaning toward prefer-tenant for srcip preservation, but worried about noisy customer bgp.
ravi: Could gate tenant-preference on stability metrics. If on-prem meets health checks, pick it; else prefer relay. keeps best of both worlds.
lee: What health checks? consecutive announce time? withdraw rate? as-path anomalies?
olivia: Proposal: require >= 45s of continuous announcement, <=1 withdraw in last 5m, and AS_PATH delta <= 2 from median.
sam: Sounds reasonable. Also add a flapping penalty: any prefix with >2 withdraws in 5m gets a significant score hit for 10m.
ops-bot: note: will emit route.precedence.evaluation with tags {tenant, prefix, selected, reason}.
ravi: Implementation sketch: compute a numeric score per candidate route. base: tenant=100, relay=90. subtract penalties: withdraws=-50, flap=-30, long-aspath=-10 per extra-hop. choose highest.
lee: Add enterprise override: config tag 'force_tenant_route=true' for paid customers who accept risk.
sam: Edge case: both routes tied after penalties. need deterministic tiebreaker to avoid nondeterministic flaps.
olivia: Tie-breaker order: higher origin-pref -> shorter AS_PATH -> lowest next-hop ip (lexicographic). Document that explicitly.
ops-bot: annotated. will log tie_breaker_reason on every decision.
ravi: Observability: expose a small histogram of score deltas and a per-tenant timeline of route.score changes. Alert if score flips >3 times in 10m.
lee: Rollout plan: behind FF 'route_precedence_scorer'. start in telemetry-only mode for 24h, then controlled canary (5% tenants), then ramp.
sam: Perf: route ingestion path will compute scores; expect ~5-8% CPU on router eval service during ramp. infra ok?
ravi: infra ok but request autoscale buffer for eval workers.
olivia: Runbook stub for support: 1) check route.precedence.evaluation events 2) inspect score history 3) verify peering health dashboard 4) if tenant needs stickiness, set force_tenant_route and monitor.
lee: Also add a small UI flag in console for enterprise admins to request stickiness (creates manual override).
ops-bot: noted: will generate alert when manual override is set.
sam: One more: store last 1h of score events for each prefix to help postmortems (compact).
ravi: ok to keep rolling 1h window in redis stream, TTL 2h.
olivia: Any objections? if none i'll put numbers into follow-up RFC and ship runbook + canary plan.
sam: no objections from networking. +1 to canary & telemetry first.
lee: sres: +1, add flip alert.
ops-bot: action: create telemetry dashboard panel 'route-precedence-flips' and a playbook link.
olivia: thanks all, will open PR with exact thresholds and rollout steps. tagging @sam @ravi for review :rocket:
